temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small, about 3 oz (90 g) 380°F / 195°C · 18 min 400°F / 205°C · 23 min Medium, 4–5 oz (130 g) 380°F / 195°C · 22 min 400°F / 205°C · 28 min Large, 6 oz (170 g) and over 380°F / 195°C · 26 min 400°F / 205°C · 33 min Safe but chewy: the drumstick trap A drumstick is the hardest-working muscle on the bird, wrapped in tendons and connective tissue. At 165°F it is safe to eat, but that tissue is still tight, so the meat clings to the bone, feels springy and can show a pink tinge at the joint even when it is fully cooked. Cooks who pull drumsticks at the breast temperature think they have undercooked them; cooks who keep going until the skin is dark often find them dry outside. The answer is to aim past the safe number on purpose. Collagen starts to melt into gelatine at about 175°F, and between there and 185°F the meat loosens, turns silky and slides off the bone. Worked example Six medium drumsticks, about 1½ lb in total, dried, rubbed with oil, garlic powder and smoked paprika. Preheat for 4 minutes, stand them in one layer with space between, and cook at 380°F for 22 minutes, turning at 11 minutes. Small legs are ready in about 18 minutes and big ones need about 26. A tray of the same drumsticks takes 400°F for around 28 minutes in a conventional oven. How to tell they are done Slide the thermometer in from the meaty top until it just touches the bone, then pull back a little. 165°F (74°C) is the safety line; 175–185°F is where drumsticks taste best. By eye, the skin should be taut and deep brown, the meat should have shrunk back to show a little of the bone at the narrow end, and the leg should twist easily at the knuckle. Pink near the bone at the right temperature is pigment, not rawness. Before they go in Dry the skin well and season generously; drumsticks are thick enough to take salt an hour ahead. Score the meat once or twice down to the bone on the thickest side so heat reaches the middle sooner. Arrange them alternating thick and thin ends. A glaze or barbecue sauce goes on only for the last two or three minutes. Related presets Chicken breast 375°F · 16 min · flip at 8 Chicken wings 400°F · 22 min · flip at 11 Chicken thighs 380°F · 24 min · flip at 12 400°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do chicken drumsticks take in the air fryer? About 22 minutes at 380°F for medium fresh drumsticks, turned at 11 minutes. Small ones take around 18 minutes and large ones around 26. What internal temperature should drumsticks reach? They are safe at 165°F (74°C), but most cooks take them to 175–185°F, where the connective tissue softens and the meat comes away from the bone. Why is my drumstick pink near the bone? Young chicken bones leak a little pigment into the surrounding meat. If the thermometer reads 165°F or more, the colour is harmless. When do I add barbecue sauce to drumsticks? In the last two or three minutes. Sugar in the sauce burns long before the legs are cooked if it goes on at the start. How does this compare with an oven? A conventional oven needs 400°F for about 28 minutes, and a fan oven 400°F for about 24. The air fryer crisps the skin noticeably more.
